## ARIMAX Robustness Results

The ARIMAX check sharpens the interpretation of the main OLS findings. For Reddit, the strongest ARIMAX row is still INTC, and the coefficient remains positive at about `0.0230`. However, the robust `p`-value rises to `0.142`, which means the coefficient no longer reaches conventional significance once autoregressive history, sector and market controls, volatility conditions, and lagged Reddit posting volume are included together. NVDA and AMD remain clearly null in the same framework.

The Bluesky ARIMAX results are even weaker. All three Bluesky firm coefficients stay close to zero, and none approaches conventional significance. This is consistent with the broader result pattern from the correlation and OLS layers: Bluesky can be processed cleanly by the pipeline, but it does not currently produce a meaningful next-day return signal under the main TabularisAI specification.

The most useful way to read the ARIMAX block is therefore as a robustness filter rather than as a contradiction of the earlier OLS result. The simple OLS rows show where the signal first becomes visible. The ARIMAX rows show that once richer time-series structure is introduced, the signal becomes more fragile and should be presented cautiously.

| Platform | Firm | Best ARIMAX order | N | Tabularis coefficient | Robust SE | $p$-value |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Reddit | `NVDA` | `(1,0,0)` | 580 | -0.0096 | 0.0108 | 0.371 |
| Reddit | `AMD` | `(1,0,0)` | 587 | 0.0047 | 0.0098 | 0.627 |
| Reddit | `INTC` | `(1,0,0)` | 585 | 0.0230 | 0.0157 | 0.142 |
| Bluesky | `NVDA` | `(1,0,0)` | 767 | 0.0045 | 0.0070 | 0.523 |
| Bluesky | `AMD` | `(1,0,0)` | 767 | -0.0016 | 0.0079 | 0.844 |
| Bluesky | `INTC` | `(1,0,0)` | 767 | 0.0014 | 0.0070 | 0.837 |

: ARIMAX robustness summary using the TabularisAI multilingual sentiment feature with AR(1) history and benchmark controls. Reddit specifications also include lagged post volume when available.

## Cross-Model Comparison

Taken together, the model comparison shows three distinct roles. FinBERT is the most stable cross-platform measurement layer, which makes it valuable for robustness and interpretation. NRC is the most variable and most lexically transparent, which makes it useful for descriptive diagnostics and emotional decomposition but less dominant in the main predictive story. The TabularisAI model provides the strongest directional firm-level result, especially for Reddit INTC, which is why the report uses it as the primary formal inference layer. At the same time, the new ARIMAX block shows that this TabularisAI advantage weakens once autoregressive history and fuller market controls are included. This division of labor across models is one of the report's most useful methodological findings, and the remaining model-specific visual detail can be shifted to the appendix without losing that core point.

# Interpretation and Limitations

## What the Results Support

The most defensible conclusion is that the pipeline itself works. The project successfully transforms a large, heterogeneous body of public social-media text into market-aligned daily sentiment features using transparent rules that are consistent across Reddit and Bluesky. That is not a trivial accomplishment. In sentiment-finance work, many apparent findings are difficult to evaluate because the path from raw text to final panel is only partially documented. Here, the stages of collection, cleaning, language handling, scoring, timing alignment, and market merging are visible enough to support a credible methodological contribution.

The results also support a second, narrower conclusion: comparable daily sentiment series can be produced from both platforms, but their empirical usefulness is not the same. The descriptive and formal results agree that Reddit yields the strongest firm-level signal in the current sample, while Bluesky remains much weaker in the present return-prediction block. That asymmetry is meaningful because it suggests that the pipeline is sensitive to real differences in platform environment rather than mechanically forcing the same result everywhere.

Finally, the report supports a modest empirical claim. A platform-specific short-run signal appears in selected Reddit specifications, most clearly in the TabularisAI sentiment measure for INTC. That result is best read as early but credible evidence, not as proof of a broad sentiment-return mechanism across all firms and platforms. The new ARIMAX results reinforce this caution by showing that the positive Reddit INTC coefficient remains visible but loses conventional significance once autoregressive history and benchmark controls are modeled jointly.

## What the Results Do Not Support

At the same time, the report does not support a claim of broad, strong, cross-platform predictability. Most of the measured relationships are small, many are indistinguishable from zero, and the clearest signal is concentrated in a limited subset of the design rather than spread uniformly across firms, models, and platforms. This is exactly why the strongest framing of the report emphasizes a working cross-platform measurement system with selective empirical success rather than a general forecasting breakthrough.

The report also does not show that all firms respond similarly to measured sentiment. NVDA, AMD, and INTC do not move together in the results, and platform-level differences further complicate the story. That heterogeneity is not a flaw, but it does mean the paper should avoid language suggesting that semiconductor sentiment operates as a single common channel across the entire sample.

More specifically, the analysis does not yet support the full later-stage hypotheses on event-window abnormal returns, volatility forecasting, or cross-firm exposure heterogeneity. Those remain plausible and well motivated, but they are not the findings established by the evidence summarized here.

## Why Effects Are Small

There are good reasons to expect the observed effects to be small. Daily stock returns are noisy outcomes that reflect a large number of overlapping information flows, many of which have nothing to do with social-media discussion. Even when public tone captures meaningful attention or concern, that information must compete with earnings news, macroeconomic conditions, sector-wide repricing, and broader risk sentiment.

The benchmark-controlled regressions make this especially clear. Once SOXX, SPY, and VIX are included, a large share of total model fit is explained by those common factors rather than by sentiment alone. The ARIMAX block pushes this one step further by allowing the model to absorb return history directly. Under that stricter specification, the TabularisAI coefficient for Reddit INTC falls from the simple OLS estimate of about `0.0480` to about `0.0230`, and the `p`-value rises from `0.014` to `0.142`. This is not surprising. Semiconductor equities are strongly tied to both sector and market conditions, and any text-based signal is likely to be incremental rather than dominant.

There is also a design reason the unconditional daily tests may understate the true relevance of policy sentiment. Export-control risk is probably most informative in narrow windows around actual policy announcements, licensing shocks, or geopolitical escalations. When the entire sample is pooled into broad daily panels, those high-information windows are mixed together with long stretches of ordinary background discussion. The report therefore provides a realistic lower-intensity test rather than the narrowest possible test of the core mechanism.

## Platform Differences

The platform differences visible in the analysis are plausibly tied to differences in user base, topic mix, and posting density. Reddit discussion is often organized around firm-specific communities and investing-related discourse, which may create a tighter connection between company-centered tone and next-day return behavior. Bluesky appears more diffuse, with broader technology commentary and a lower density of focused investor-style discussion for the same focal firms.

This difference in discourse structure can matter even when the same sentiment model is applied. A classifier may be detecting real tone on both platforms, but the economic meaning of that tone can still differ if one platform is more tightly anchored to investor interpretation and the other is more conversational or generalized. In that sense, the platform effect is not just a nuisance variable. It is part of the substantive result.

The report therefore treats Reddit's stronger performance not as proof that Reddit is inherently superior, but as evidence that platform-specific community structure may influence whether public sentiment becomes statistically visible in short-horizon equity tests.

## Measurement and Scope Limits

The report also faces several measurement limits that should be acknowledged explicitly. Keyword-based collection is necessary for a project of this scale, but it inevitably introduces some noise. Not every matched post is equally relevant to export-control risk, and some discussion may enter the sample because it mentions a company or technology term without contributing to the policy-risk channel of greatest interest. The Tier 1 versus Tier 2 structure helps address this problem, but it does not eliminate it completely.

Sampling and platform-history limits also matter. Reddit and Bluesky are not perfect mirrors of the same population, and they are not observed over identical periods or under identical levels of activity. Some of the platform difference in the results may therefore reflect sample composition as much as true economic difference. In addition, sentiment models themselves are imperfect measurement tools. Even a multilingual transformer or finance-domain classifier can misread sarcasm, policy nuance, or mixed-intensity discussion.

Most importantly, the report stops short of claiming completion of the full policy-event and volatility agenda. Narrow event-study estimation, realized-volatility forecasting, and exposure-heterogeneity tests remain the most logical extensions. The analysis establishes the infrastructure and the first empirical layer needed to pursue those designs, but later stages are not presented as completed.

# Conclusion

## Main Takeaways

The main takeaway from this report is that the project successfully builds a reusable cross-platform NLP pipeline for semiconductor export-control sentiment measurement. The workflow collects public text from Reddit and Bluesky, applies common cleaning and timing rules, scores posts with three sentiment systems, and produces daily market-aligned features suitable for empirical analysis. That methodological contribution is substantial on its own because it responds directly to the data-fragility problem that motivated the original UROP proposal.

The second takeaway is empirical but deliberately modest. The daily sentiment-return relationship is generally weak, model-dependent, and platform-sensitive. Reddit produces the clearest evidence of a short-run firm-level relationship, especially under the TabularisAI measure for INTC, while Bluesky does not generate statistically significant return-predictive results in the current specifications. The new ARIMAX robustness block keeps the same directional ordering but weakens the Reddit INTC result once autoregressive dynamics and common market controls are modeled jointly. The report therefore contributes both a working research tool and a disciplined account of where measurable signal appears strongest and where it becomes fragile.

## Extensions Beyond the Present Report

The most direct extension is a narrow event-study design centered on specific BIS announcements, export-control revisions, Entity List actions, or related semiconductor-policy shocks. That design would test the risk-premium hypothesis in a setting where the policy channel is most likely to be visible.

Another extension is volatility forecasting. Because the theoretical motivation of the project includes an uncertainty channel, realized-volatility models over 1- to 5-day windows may prove more informative than unconditional daily return tests. Existing notes about ARIMAX-style extensions and volatility targets provide a reasonable starting point for that phase.

Third, the report can be extended into a formal exposure-heterogeneity design. The broader semiconductor universe and exposure logic already exist conceptually, but the analysis does not yet estimate whether high-exposure firms systematically respond more strongly than lower-exposure firms. That comparative step would move the project closer to a stronger sector-wide conclusion.

Finally, additional attention proxies such as Google Trends or related search-volume measures could complement the sentiment variables and help distinguish tone from raw attention. These are extensions rather than necessities, but they would be useful if the project develops into a longer paper.

## Final Closing Sentence

Taken together, the evidence suggests that this project has already succeeded as a methodological contribution and has also uncovered promising but limited early evidence that public semiconductor sentiment, especially on Reddit, can align with short-run market outcomes under carefully structured measurement and timing rules.

## Appendix F. Granger, Stationarity, and PCA

This appendix is the right home for exploratory diagnostics that should not dominate the central narrative:

- Granger causality summaries
- ADF or stationarity checks
- PCA and feature-space plots
- any additional lead-lag or exploratory correlation-function outputs

These diagnostics are still valuable because they document what was checked, even where they do not carry the main conclusion.

$$
r_t=\alpha+\sum_{\ell=1}^{p}\phi_{\ell}r_{t-\ell}+\sum_{\ell=1}^{p}\theta_{\ell}S_{t-\ell}+u_t
$$

$$
H_0:\theta_1=\theta_2=\cdots=\theta_p=0
$$

| Symbol | Definition |
|---|---|
| $r_t$ | Return series at time $t$ |
| $S_t$ | Sentiment series at time $t$ |
| $\phi_{\ell}$ | Autoregressive coefficients on lagged returns |
| $\theta_{\ell}$ | Granger coefficients on lagged sentiment |
| $p$ | Maximum lag order tested |
| $H_0$ | Null hypothesis that sentiment does not Granger-cause returns |

: Variable definitions for the Granger-causality test.

| Platform | Direction tested | Wald $p$-value | Conclusion at 5 percent |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Reddit | sentiment $\rightarrow$ equal-weighted return | 0.809 | Fail to reject |
| Reddit | equal-weighted return $\rightarrow$ sentiment | 0.206 | Fail to reject |
| Bluesky | sentiment $\rightarrow$ equal-weighted return | 0.600 | Fail to reject |
| Bluesky | equal-weighted return $\rightarrow$ sentiment | 0.771 | Fail to reject |
